title: Qt: Copy as HTML
description:
**Summary**

This feature introduces an option to copy in HTML format via main menu, context menu and keyboard shortcut. It also provides an option to copy plain text with aligned columns along with an ability to select a copy format to be used when copied via keyboard shortcut.

**HTML Format**

- Packet list is copied in HTML table format with following preset styling.
  - Font (name-n-size) used by Wireshark is used.
  - Header row is white-on-black and its columns are left-aligned.
  - Distance between text and its border is half of the font size (in pt).
- Data is aligned either left or right as per displayed columns in packet list.
- Packet list is copied in plain text format too for text-only editors. Note: Plain text is aligned if column alignment is selected in preferences.
  * Preference: gui_packet_list_copy_text_with_aligned_columns
  * Value: true/false
  * Default: false (to maintain compatibility with existing copy-paste) Important: Though standard HTML is used, some WYSIWYG editors could choose to partially implement or skip a particular feature.

**Keyboard Shortcut**

- User can choose default format to be used.
  * Preference: gui_packet_list_copy_format_options_for_keyboard_shortcut
  * Value: Text, CSV, YAML and HTML
  * Default: Text (to maintain compatibility with existing copy-paste)
- If HTML is selected, then plain text is also copied for text-only editors.
  - If column alignment is selected, then plain text is aligned accordingly.

**Minor Fixes**

- New line has been added to text and CSV when copied via context menu and also to text when copied via keyboard shortcut.
- New line before "---" in YAML has been removed which is present from second packet when multiple packets are copied.

**Question** - Should headers in HTML output be aligned too (if possible)? _(because current UI does not do so)_

**Question** - Should packet numbers be fixed in YAML output? _(not sure if this was intended, but current YAML output shows that packet numbers in "# Packet" comment (for each packet) are zero-based and are not impacted by filtering)_

* **What are the UI changes made by this MR?**
  * It adds `As HTML` to main menu and `...as HTML` to context menu as shown in Figure 1A and 1B respectively.
* **What are the "Preferences" added by this MR?**
  * A choice preference `gui_packet_list_copy_format_options_for_keyboard_shortcut` and a bool preference `gui_packet_list_copy_text_with_aligned_columns` are added as shown in Figure 2A. Figure 2B shows the choices available for keyboard shortcut.
* **Does it change the existing copy behavior?**
  * No unless the defaults are changed.

    > Existing copy behavior is to copy data _(packet summary or displayed packet list)_ in the format selected. When the format of `Plain Text` or `CSV` is selected via main menu, header is copied along with the data but when the same is selected via context menu or keyboard shortcut, only the data is copied.
* **What are those defaults?**
  * `Text` as the default format when selected via keyboard shortcut (CTRL+C or CMD+C) and to use tab as the delimiter when `Text` format is used irrespective from where it is selected _(main menu, context menu or keyboard shortcut)_.
* **Are there any screenshots available that show the features in action?**
  * Yes. Figure 3A shows Wireshark with font information. Figure 3B shows OneNote, Figure 3C shows Outlook/Word and Figure 3D shows text with tab delimiter and space delimiter + column alignment. 

    > Do note that an HTML Table could be pasted bit differently in different applications depending on what styles are accepted and how it should be processed. For example, OneNote will not draw a border by default but when asked, it will draw a single line border even though `border-collapse` style property is not present. And a consecutive paste _(of the same content - HTML Table)_ will create a new table right below the existing one even though the cursor is on the last column of pasted content. Whereas Outlook/Word will show the borders as expected but consecutive paste will become a row of earlier table even though the cursor is on a new line. Writer from LibreOffice and NobleNote also show different behaviors in respect to cursor location and consecutive paste, but the end result is that an HTML Table is copied with color and font information as seen in the Wireshark.
